The event occurred around 8 p.m. near the Sugar & Spice Restaurant on Route 4. According to police, Altahan was driving westbound when her GPS system suddenly instructed her to turn around, as the car had passed its intended destination. Reacting swiftly to the directions, she attempted to make the turn, which caused the car to leave the traffic lane and become entangled with the guy wire supporting a telephone pole.  

Although the incident was unexpected, neither Altahan nor her passenger sustained any injuries. A witness at a nearby miniature golf course reported seeing the driver exit the vehicle as it was suspended from the pole. The scene was responded to by State Police and the Rutland City Fire Department, who arrived to assist. Ray Ault, who was driving by the area at the time, provided an account of the event.  

This incident highlights the potential risks of relying too heavily on GPS navigation systems, particularly when drivers react quickly to sudden or unexpected directions. While the outcome was fortunate in terms of avoiding injury, it serves as a reminder of the importance of careful driving and the need to remain vigilant when using technology while on the road.
